new.analysis:
Week one went the way a return from a stress reaction should. All three sessions held pain at 0/10 and the shin was quiet afterward. Every minute with a heart rate reading was in zones 1 and 2, and drift within each session stayed small, between -3.5 and +3.6 bpm.

Your pace splits show how the sessions were built. Running segments sat near 6:45/km and walking near 10:30/km, which fits five rounds of about 1 min running and 2 min walking. That is roughly 5 min of running per session and 15 min across the week. If you did it differently, tell me in your next check-in, because the plan builds on that number.

I am changing running minutes only, and by very little. Your fitness will come back faster than your shin's tolerance for load, so the limit is about 10 percent more running minutes a week. One extra minute of running, from 15 to 16 minutes across the week, sits inside that limit. Run pace and the length of each running segment stay where they are for now.

That rate of progress moves the October target. A single 30 min run is nearly twice all the running you will do next week. At about 10 percent a week, getting there takes months, not five weeks. I would rather give you an honest later date than push the shin to meet this one.

The order from here is more rounds, then longer running segments, and pace last. Strides, hills and faster running wait until you have four pain-free weeks in a row. Your 40 km weeks before the injury are not the reference point now. The last few weeks of shin history are.

Use the same rules each morning after a run. Pain at 3/10 or below that settles by the next morning allows the next small step. Pain above 3/10 during a run, or a shin that is worse the next morning, means repeating or shortening the last session. In that case, let your physio know before you run again.

settingsProposalBullets: Keep your running days at Monday, Wednesday and Saturday, as your physio set them, until your physio says otherwise.
Keep every run easy, with no strides, hills or intervals, until four pain-free weeks in a row. One week is counted so far.
Replace "30 minutes without walking by mid-October" with a staged goal: build running minutes first, and set the 30 minute date later.
Your walk-run session is 5 rounds of about 1 min running and 2 min walking. Tell me if that is wrong.
Stop the run if the shin aches, and tell your physio if the ache comes back the next morning.
